text: A portfolio has an expected annual return of 10.40%, a standard deviation of 24.55%, and the risk-free rate is 2.96%. Calculate the Sharpe Ratio.
An investor allocates 73% of a portfolio to Asset A (expected return 5.38%) and 27% to Asset B (expected return 5.07%). Calculate the expected portfolio return as a decimal (e.g. 0.05 for 5%).
Asset A has a standard deviation of 8.57% and Asset B has a standard deviation of 14.32%. The covariance between the two assets is -0.003793. Calculate the correlation coefficient between A and B.

A stock traded at $140.88 at the start of the year and at $167.38 at the end of the year (no dividends paid). The annualized standard deviation of returns is 10.99% and the risk-free rate is 1.42%. First calculate the annual return, then calculate the Sharpe Ratio.
